title: Exploring the Credit Card Fraud Data Set

cues.en: Welcome to Section two Introduction to Fraud Detection.
cues.zh: 歡迎來到第二章：詐欺偵測簡介。

cues.en: This is Lecture five exploring the credit card fraud dataset.
cues.zh: 這是第五堂課：探索信用卡詐欺資料集。

cues.en: So I've provided a link to the web page on Kaggle that contains the credit card fraud dataset that the
cues.zh: 我已提供 Kaggle 網頁連結，裡面有信用卡詐欺資料集，

cues.en: authors of this Machine Learning Research group have luckily provided.
cues.zh: 很幸運，這個機器學習研究團隊的作者願意提供這份資料。

cues.en: It's in the public domain, so we can just grab it off of Kaggle.
cues.zh: 資料已公開，因此可以直接從 Kaggle 取得。

cues.en: If you don't know what Kaggle is, it's a website that hosts machine learning competitions.
cues.zh: 如果你不知道 Kaggle，它是一個舉辦機器學習競賽的網站。

cues.en: There are a lot of datasets.
cues.zh: 上面有很多資料集。

cues.en: There's a lot of notebooks, interactive notebooks that contain solutions to problems.
cues.zh: 也有許多包含問題解法的互動式 Notebook。

cues.en: Organizations and groups also holds machine learning competitions, and then people provide solutions they submit.
cues.zh: 組織或團體會在上面舉辦機器學習競賽，參賽者則提交自己的解法。

cues.en: There can be prize money to be won for for certain competitions.
cues.zh: 有些競賽還設有獎金。

cues.en: So, yeah, it's a great place to look at really good machine learning models that people develop to
cues.zh: 所以，它很適合用來研究其他人開發的優秀機器學習模型，

cues.en: find access to really good datasets.
cues.zh: 也能找到很好的資料集。

cues.en: And it's just a nice central repository for all these things that you that you might want to use within your machine learning journey.
cues.zh: 它把機器學習學習歷程中可能用到的各種資源，集中在同一個地方。

cues.en: Okay, so we are going to now use pandas within Python to interrogate and understand what the data actually looks like.
cues.zh: 接下來，我們會使用 Python 的 pandas，檢視並了解這份資料的實際樣貌。

cues.en: So we're going to be using pandas.
cues.zh: 我們會用到 pandas。

cues.en: And I'm going to use the pandas dot read CSV method to read in the CSV file, assuming that the directory
cues.zh: 透過 pandas 的 read_csv 方法讀取 CSV 檔，這裡假設該檔案

cues.en: is in the same folder as my notebook.
cues.zh: 與 Notebook 放在同一個資料夾。

cues.en: And I'm just going to assign that to a variable called DF for dataframe.
cues.zh: 我會把讀取結果指定給 df 這個變數，代表 DataFrame。

cues.en: And then once that's done, if I want to see what the data frame looks like, I can just print the head,
cues.zh: 完成後，如果想看看 DataFrame 的樣子，可以輸出 head，

cues.en: which will just give me a snapshot of the top five rows as well as all of the columns in the in the data frame.
cues.zh: 它會顯示前五列以及 DataFrame 中的所有欄位。

cues.en: And if I wanted to do some more high level descriptive statistics, I can use dataframe dot describe
cues.zh: 如果想做更高層次的描述統計，可以使用 DataFrame 的 describe 方法，

cues.en: and that will actually tell me what the, you know, count the mean standard deviation and the max, that kind of thing.
cues.zh: 查看筆數、平均數、標準差、最大值等資訊。

cues.en: For each of the numeric columns within the data frame, all of them are numerical, so they all do show up.
cues.zh: 這會針對 DataFrame 中每個數值欄位計算；目前所有欄位都是數值，所以全部都會顯示。

cues.en: But if you've got some categorical or text based columns and things like that, it won't include it in the output of the describe method.
cues.zh: 但如果有類別或文字欄位，describe 方法預設的輸出就不會包含它們。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So we see that there are 31 columns within this data frame.
cues.zh: 這個 DataFrame 有 31 個欄位。

cues.en: There are 284,000 records or rows and the features they are expressed at the transaction level, right?
cues.zh: 共有約 284,000 筆紀錄，也就是資料列，而且特徵是在交易層級表示的。

cues.en: So they're not aggregated at the user level, rather at the transaction level, but a single user might have multiple transactions.
cues.zh: 它們不是在使用者層級彙整，而是在交易層級；同一位使用者可能會有多筆交易。

cues.en: You know, these could just be credit card swipes, for example, and they include features such as the transaction amount.
cues.zh: 例如，這些紀錄可能就是每次刷卡的資料，包含交易金額等特徵。

cues.en: So the amount that was, you know, swiped for the time of the transaction and a number of features
cues.zh: 也就是刷卡金額、交易時間，以及一組

cues.en: or columns called V one through V 28.
cues.zh: 從 V1 到 V28 的特徵欄位。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: And we know because they are research papers associated with this data set, the authors have claimed
cues.zh: 根據這個資料集所附的研究論文，作者表示

cues.en: that the features have been derived from a process called principal component analysis, which is effectively
cues.zh: 這些特徵是經過主成分分析，也就是 PCA 所得到的；

cues.en: an approach for reducing the dimensionality of the data.
cues.zh: 它是一種降低資料維度的方法。

cues.en: So what that means is the data set was likely a lot wider.
cues.zh: 也就是說，原始資料集可能寬得多。

cues.en: So the size of the feature space was a lot broader.
cues.zh: 原本的特徵空間可能更大。

cues.en: You know, there might have been 100 features, for example, then apply PCA to reduce that number down to the 28 of them, which is great.
cues.zh: 例如，原先可能有 100 個特徵，套用 PCA 後，將數量降成目前的 28 個，這很不錯。

cues.en: The only problem is that it removes the interpretability aspect.
cues.zh: 唯一的問題是，這會降低可解釋性。

cues.en: It makes it difficult to understand exactly what these features kind of represent.
cues.zh: 我們不容易確切了解這些特徵代表什麼。

cues.en: You know, we can train a model and then post-hoc understand, well, which of these contributed to
cues.zh: 我們可以先訓練模型，再事後分析哪些特徵

cues.en: the modeling decision, you know, which ones contributed most to the detection of fraudulent records.
cues.zh: 影響了模型的判斷，例如哪些特徵對辨識詐欺紀錄最有幫助。

cues.en: But at the end of the day, we don't actually know what this v four means or what this v three means, for example.
cues.zh: 但到頭來，我們其實不知道 V4 或 V3 本身代表什麼。

cues.en: Right, but they obviously still are proven to be informative features.
cues.zh: 不過，這些特徵顯然仍已證明含有有用資訊。

cues.en: So they will help us to detect instances of fraud within this dataset.
cues.zh: 因此，它們仍能幫助我們偵測這個資料集中的詐欺案例。
